Subject: Intermittent connection failures to PrivateLink endpoint during peak

Hi Evelyn,

We started seeing intermittent failures to the PrivateLink endpoint (pl-01.acme.redwood.local) during yesterday's payment batch. Symptoms: repeated SYN_RETRIES from our frontend to the PrivateLink IPs, followed by long stalls and then packet retransmits. Packet captures show a lot of fragmented TCP segments and occasional ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages that never make it back to the sender.

We suspect something changed on the transit uplink (our side) after a config push to the NGFW earlier this week, but we don't want to assume. Attaching a small pcap (acme_peak_pcap_snippet.pcap) and a traceroute (traceroute_private_link.txt) that show the path and the MTU hints.

Can Redwood triage from the PrivateLink perspective? The issue is impacting transaction throughput and we'd like to get a mutually-agreed mitigation plan before the next batch at 21:00 PT.

Attachments: acme_peak_pcap_snippet.pcap (pcap), traceroute_private_link.txt (txt)

Thanks,
Maria Garcia
NetOps Engineer | Acme Payments

Thanks Maria — appreciate the pcap and traceroute. I'm pulling in Jonás (networking) and Marissa (private deployments) to help.

High-level plan:
- Initial triage (Jonás): confirm whether PrivateLink endpoint is receiving DF/ICMP errors and whether SGs are dropping ICMP frag-needed.
- Short mitigation: apply an MTU clamp on the PrivateLink endpoint pair and add temporary egress SG rule to allow ICMP-type 3/code 4 (fragmentation needed).
- Long-term: identify where along the transit path ICMP replies are being dropped (customer NGFW vs transit) and update recommended MTU or routing accordingly.

Jonás/Marissa — can you review the pcap and propose a safe change window? Maria, if you can share the NGFW rule snapshot (or confirm whether ICMP is blocked), that will help.

—Evelyn

Subject: Re: Intermittent connection failures to PrivateLink endpoint during peak

Thanks — I pulled the pcap. Quick notes from initial triage:

- I see multiple TCP segments with the Don't Fragment (DF) bit set followed by ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation needed) messages originating from an intermediate hop, but the ICMP replies appear to be asymmetric or dropped before reaching the Acme frontend. That pattern = PMTU discovery failure (blackhole).
- Possible causes: NGFW on Acme's edge dropping/inspecting ICMP, transit device MTU mismatch (jumbo frames on one side), or an intermediate NAT that rewrites headers and drops frag-needed replies.
- Also noticed a handful of TCP resets where MSS negotiation indicates 1460; if PMTU is lower, that will cause fragmentation attempts and stalls.

Immediate recommendations (safe, reversible):
1) Allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 on the path (temporary rule) so PMTU discovery can complete. If Acme can't allow it globally, allow it between the Acme frontend ranges and the PrivateLink subnets.
2) Apply an MTU clamp on the PrivateLink veth/tunnel endpoint to 1438 (safe starting point) to avoid fragmentation while we trace the path.
3) Collect tcpdump with the packet size filter on both sides: 
   - Acme: tcpdump -s 0 -w acme_side.pcap 'tcp and (len > 1400)'
   - Redwood endpoint: sudo tcpdump -i pl-eth -s 0 -w redwood_side.pcap 'tcp and (len > 1400)'

If you approve, Marissa and I can schedule a 20-minute window to apply the clamp and add the temporary SG/ACL allow. We will have rollback steps if traffic changes are negative.

Jonás Weber
Senior Network Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonás — I confirmed with our NGFW team and they did push a tightening rule earlier this week that blocks most ICMP types by default. They're willing to add a scoped rule to allow Type 3 Code 4 between our frontend ranges (10.12.0.0/16) and your PrivateLink subnets for the test window.

We can approve the MTU clamp on the PrivateLink endpoint for the 21:00 PT batch window if Redwood will implement and monitor, and if you have a rollback. Also attached is the traceroute I ran earlier showing the hop where DF/frag-needed appears to originate.

Attachments: traceroute_private_link.txt

Subject: Re: Intermittent connection failures to PrivateLink endpoint during peak

Hi all — Redwood will implement the short mitigation as follows:

Planned changes (canary first, 15-minute window):
- Step 1 (canary endpoint): apply MTU clamp to 1438 on one PrivateLink endpoint instance and add SG rule to allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 from Acme frontend ranges.
- Step 2 (monitor): monitor connection success and token throughput for 10 minutes.
- Step 3 (rollout): if stable, roll the config across the pair.

Rollback plan: remove MTU clamp and revoke the temporary SG rule; traffic will return to prior state. We'll take packet captures concurrently and will provide them.

I've attached a short runbook (redwood_runbook_privatelink_patch.pdf) with the exact CLI steps and rollback commands. Proposed window: 21:00-21:30 PT today. Please confirm acceptance and whether Acme will coordinate the NGFW scoped ICMP allow at the same time.

—Marissa Cole

Thank you for the fast turnaround and the clear rollback plan. We'll follow up internally to evaluate a permanent NGFW rule change or an upstream transit MTU reconciliation, but for now this mitigates the immediate customer impact.

Marking this as resolved from our side.
